7._section_summary: This section presents the results of a principal-axis factor analysis of the BAS-2 (Body Appreciation Scale-2) instrument. The analysis indicated adequate factorability (Bartlett's test p < .001, KMO = .93) and revealed that a single factor should be extracted, with an eigenvalue of 5.69 explaining 56.89% of total variance. All 10 BAS-2 items loaded onto this single factor with fair to excellent factor loadings.

12._section_summary: This discussion section presents findings from a single study examining the psychometric properties of an Arabic-translated version of the BAS-2 administered to young adult female university students in the UAE. The study found a one-dimensional factor structure consistent with the original English version and other translations, with evidence of internal consistency and convergent validity; body appreciation scores were positively correlated with authentic body pride and body image, while the correlation with BMI was negative but not statistically significant. The authors acknowledge limitations including the use of convenience sampling of females only, reliance on self-reported BMI data, and the specificity of the sample to Arabic-speaking university women in the UAE.

1._section_summary: This section presents psychometric analyses for the BAS-2 (Body Appreciation Scale-2) using data from N=256 participants. Cronbach's alpha coefficients ranged from .89 to .92, indicating good to excellent reliability. Convergent validity was assessed through Pearson correlations, showing significant positive correlations between BAS-2 and body pride (r=.467) and body image (r=.459), but a non-significant negative correlation with BMI (r=-.04).
